::: {.why}
Your engine is now good enough to be worth comparing against ones that have run real money, and the differences are the specification for the next two phases.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name three things a production backtester does that yours does not, and say which of the three you actually need.
- Decide, in writing, what you will not build and why.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the architecture pages of NautilusTrader's documentation and the LEAN engine's, far enough to see how each separates data, execution and portfolio. Both are designed to run the same strategy code in backtest and live, which is a property your engine should have by phase 10.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the comparison and the decision: three things they do that you do not, three things your engine does that a general framework cannot easily do because it knows your data model, and the list of features you are deliberately not building. That last list is the one an interviewer will find most credible.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Note the one property to adopt now rather than later: the same strategy object should run against a historical data source or a live one, differing only in what feeds it.
:::
:::
